versions.changelog: Quiet Vercel polls no longer leak their notes into the chat: OpenClaw delivers stderr alongside NO_REPLY, so a successful scheduled run now writes its notes to web-observer.log beside the state file. Error alerts name the project and its domain and list each distinct error once, with count, routes, status, whether it was an HTTP failure, and a sample request id. Opted-in log messages are cut to one line, capped, and have common secret shapes redacted.

Watch several sites: vercel.projects and ga4.properties take lists in place of the singular keys, which still work. Each Vercel project is polled separately with its own alert state; a 0.1.1 state file carries over to the first project. The GA4 digest gets one section per property, and a failing property no longer holds back the rest.

Security hardening: Vercel error alerts no longer quote request paths chosen by whoever made the request; https-to-http redirects are refused; configured headers go only to the watch's own host. SKILL.md now declares exactly which openclaw.json keys the Vercel and GA4 modules read, and drops an undefined security_level field.
